label: bot play (forceteki rung3:k=8,det=4,belief=known), relative comparison on identical shuffles, not a human or tournament win rate
calibration: rung3:k=8,det=4,belief=known: calibration unmeasured (#183). Every measured computer player fails the outside check against real tournament results: Spearman about -0.2 against swumetastats (D88, #128). They overrate fast, aggressive decks and underrate careful ones, so these figures rank what computer players do well. Read them beside the judges' scores, never instead of them.

design: D108's relative design per idea: the idea against its leader's reference on identical seeds in both seat orders, the idea against itself on the same seeds as a mirror, and the idea and the reference against every panel list on the same seed and seat, the paired difference weighted by the panel's tournament shares; ranked by the low end of that difference's 95% bootstrap interval; the dead-card control of each reference runs as one more idea

deckMinusVariant.method: share-weighted strata, percentile bootstrap over pairs within each stratum (2000 resamples)

field.design: both decks played the same opponent list, engine seed and seat in every game; only pairs both decks decided count; the difference is deck minus variant, the share-weighted mean over strata of wins only the deck had minus wins only the variant had, per pair

pooledPairs.weighting: exact two-sided sign test with every pair counted once; each stratum was sampled with the same n, so small archetypes weigh more than in the field and this figure can disagree with deckMinusVariant, which weights strata by field share
